jobs.title: Interim Water Quality Program Specialist
jobs.description:
Job Description:


The Interim Water Quality Program Specialist (WQPS) performs complex tasks to assist with compliance of water quality regulations and programs. Primary responsibilities focus on drinking water public health, regulatory planning and compliance. Capital project support including Division of Drinking Water (DDW) permitting, developing compliance strategy, and new regulation implementation for capital projects. This includes water quality support during the general rate case development, integration of new water systems for new business efforts, and partner state projects. The WQPS will also be responsible for providing ongoing backup and coverage for the Water Quality Program Manager (WQPM) team during emergencies or personnel transitions. This position is located in East Los Angeles, CA.**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Reviews of Monitoring Schedules, permit monitoring requirements, DDW web site, analytical results of raw/finished water and sample tracking, and coordination to ensure regulatory compliance
* Assists WQPM with creation of Consumer Confidence Reports, Annual Water Quality reports, Monthly reporting, and any other internal and external reporting
* Understand permits conditions, including operations plans for distribution and treatment facilities and update plans as required
* Serves as the primary water quality stakeholder to provide input and support to the Engineering department project management process of key capital projects
* Provides WQ support for all capital projects **–** to include planning, permitting, implementation, final DDW inspections, and training
* Works as water quality lead with Engineering to develop priorities, schedule, and justifications for General Rate Case
* Supports capital planning for deficiencies from the Division of Drinking Water (DDW) Sanitary Surveys (inspections) and incorporation of water quality deficiencies in to a tracking program and monitor and prioritize for completion
* Assists WQPM in developing water quality monitoring schedules for sources, water treatment plants, and distribution systems in accordance with applicable regulations
* Supports of partner state water quality projects and integration/implementation of new water systems for new business
* Completes new water supply source data review and appropriate treatment technologies review for removal of contaminants under the direction of the WQPM and Manager of WQ
* Participates in training and presentation techniques, including media training
* Develops reports, technical summaries, and data summaries to assist with water quality studies, treatment system design review, and permitting
* Coordinates within Water Quality Department, other Departments, and Districts to ensure regulatory requirements are met
* Exhibits behavior that supports a safety culture; attends and participates at all required safety training programs; adheres to Company Safety Policies; uses Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) as appropriate, reports safety issues/concerns to management in a timely manner, and encourages others to behave in the same manner
* Participates in and supports the Company’s Continuous Improvement program and projects
* Performs work onsite at assigned office location
* Performs other similar duties as assigned

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor’s degree with major coursework in Chemistry, Biology, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field or equivalent experience
* California Division of Drinking Water Distribution Operator Grade 2 Certification within 1 year of employment
* California Division of Drinking Water Treatment Operator Grade 2 Certification within 1 year of employment
* Valid California Driver License
* Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with internal customers, outside vendors, and consultants
* Knowledge of applicable drinking water laws and regulations to include SDWA, Title 22, and Title 17
* Knowledge of internal Policy and Procedures related to drinking water, safety, and operations support
* Ability to prepare manage and analyze data
* Strong knowledge of and experience in project management
* Good interpersonal skills
* Strong problem\-solving, troubleshooting, and decision\-making skills

**Salary Range: $74,600 \- $138,400 (DOE)**

**Deadline to submit resume is Tuesday, August 11, 2026\.**


The Equal Opportunity Policy of the Company is based upon the philosophy that all people should be treated fairly and with dignity. California Water Service, Hawai'i Water Service, New Mexico Water Service, Texas Water Service and Washington Water Service do not discriminate against any applicant or employee because of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, or any other protected class. The Company makes all employment decisions in a non\-discriminatory manner. EOE, VET, DISABILITIES.

jobs.title: ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST
jobs.description:
Job Posting: Northern Lands, Program Coordinator



Department of Fish and Wildlife


JC\-526357* 

Northern Lands, Program Coordinator
  

ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST
$4,418\.00 \- $9,321\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **8/6/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


The Department is seeking a skilled and motivated land management professional to lead the stewardship of ecological reserves and other State lands, with the primary duty station at the Ballona Wetlands Ecological Reserve. This role supports the long\-term conservation of California’s natural resources through field operations, staff leadership, habitat restoration, and coordination with agency partners and the public. In this position, the selected candidate will oversee daily maintenance of Department\-managed lands, ensuring that facilities, trails, signage, fences, and infrastructure remain safe and functional for public and operational use. You’ll work alongside permanent and seasonal staff, contractors, and volunteer crews, helping ensure the lands are maintained in a collaborative effort. Duties include vegetation management, invasive species control, equipment oversight, and timely completion of routine and emergency maintenance tasks (e.g., equipment repair needs, perimeter fencing issues, addressing water leaks, etc.). You will prepare and implement adaptive management plans; conduct biological surveys; analyze habitat and species data; and assess management needs for restored, mitigation, and sensitive areas. The role includes reviewing environmental documents, obtaining necessary permits, and representing the Department on cooperative management teams and technical working groups. The position requires strong coordination with federal, State, and local agencies, neighboring landowners, land trusts and other non\-governmental organizations, volunteer groups, and academic partners. You will administer contracts, monitor funded programs, prepare reports and budgets, maintain program documentation, and help coordinate hiring and training efforts of support staff. This role involves both fieldwork and office duties, often in variable weather and rugged terrain. Overnight travel will be required up to 10%. Work hours may be 10\+ hours per day, including some night and weekend work, and may occur during varied weather conditions.  

  

  



**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:  

Personal Leave Program \- Human Resources \- CalHR.  

  

  

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in\-person at least four (4\) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N\-22\-25\. Additional in\-office days may be required based on operational needs.  

  

  

Link to Class Title Exam: Environmental Scientist*/***Exam Bulletin**  

  

**This position is posted in the following counties:** *Los Angeles/Ventura counties*. **Please apply to each county in which you are interested in working.**
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


Office will be located at Ballona Wetlands Ecological Reserve in Los Angeles OR the Cienega Springs Ecological Reserve in Fillmore. Work is conducted in office and outdoors environments, and includes highway and off\-road driving, which incorporates trail and off\-trail navigation. Driving up to 30% is an essential requirement for this position and requires a valid driver’s license, as the CDFW properties under its management require regular site visits. Many of these properties are in remote areas and span across three counties, making alternative transportation impractical. Overnight travel will be required up to 10%. Work hours may be 10\+ hours per day, including some night and weekend work, and may occur during varied weather conditions. Uniform is required when interacting with the public and while conducting fieldwork.

Department of Fish and Wildlife


JC\-526330* 

Energy Supervisor
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)
$10,854\.00 \- $13,493\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **8/6/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


The Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW), Inland Deserts Region has an exciting opportunity for an outgoing, independent, and highly motivated Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) \- to serve as an integral part of a team implementing the Habitat Conservation Planning Program working on Renewable Energy Projects and Conservation and Mitigation Banks in the Inland Deserts Region.  

  

  

The Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) will for be responsible for supervising and directing the work of staff focused on permitting of energy projects within the Inland Deserts Region including; California Endangered Species Act (CESA) early consultation and issuance of Incidental Take Permits (ITPs); Lake and Streambed Alteration (LSA) permitting, Conservation and Mitigation Banking (CMB) review, approval and implementation and California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review. This work includes supporting direct reports with early pre\-consultation, education, and outreach efforts, to proactively address potential project issues with applicants for a more expedited and efficient environmental review process.

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Specialist
jobs.description:
Riverside, CA
Full Time
EHS
Mid Level  

**Summary**


The Environmental Compliance Specialist is responsible for driving environmental compliance programs, conducting inspections and risk assessments, coordinating environmental activities, and leading training and corrective actions. This role emphasizes technical support, regulatory knowledge, and cross\-functional collaboration without direct management responsibilities.

**Essential Functions of the Job**

  

* Manage and oversee local, state, and federal environmental regulations and Luxfer policy. Proactively research and maintain awareness of changes in regulations and facilitate communication with relevant stakeholders.
* Drive an environmentally responsible culture within the organization. Develop and execute programs through partnerships with engineering, maintenance, and operations.
* Maintain and enhance the facilities ISO 14001 Certification
* Lead regulatory agency interactions, permit evaluation and processing, and new process and technology introduction.
* Ensure work performed by contractors, consultants, and employees is completed in accordance with Luxfer standards.
* Drive environmental metrics
* Build collaborative relationships with various stakeholders to ensure risks are identified early and managed appropriately.
* Submit time\-critical reports to various governmental agencies.
* Complete thorough and accurate environmental incident investigations and accompanying regulatory reports and develop appropriate corrective actions.
* Conduct regular environmental audits to assess compliance, identify areas for improvement, and implement corrective actions in collaboration with local operations leadership and teams.
* Develops and oversees waste management programs, including hazardous waste disposal.
* Provide training to employees on environmental policies, procedures, and best practices, fostering a culture of environmental responsibility.
* Coordinates environmental impact assessments for new projects, operations, or changes to existing processes, ensuring potential environmental risks are identified and mitigated.
* Prepare and submit required environmental reports to regulatory agencies, stakeholders, and internal management.
* Partner with Safety Manager on overlapping programs. Serve as a back\-up for Safety Manager.

**Job Skills and Requirements**

* Technical Knowledge of EPA Regulations, Hazardous Waste Management, relevant Environmental Programs (including but not limited to SWPPP, SPCC, HAZCOM), Environmental Permits and Recordkeeping
* Strong Analytical and problem\-solving skills.
* Attention to detail
* ISO 14001 Internal Auditor Certification Preferred
* Strong project management and organizational skills
* Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities.
* Certifications in environmental management (e.g., CEM, CHMM) are a plus.
* Strong knowledge and utilization of Microsoft Office products.
* Experience with CERS and SMARTS CA specific web based environmental solutions

**Education/Training Requirements**

* 3\+ years of increasing responsibilities in environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations experience
* Bachelor's Degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Engineering, or related field of study highly preferred.

  



***BENEFITS:***

* Medical, Vision, Dental \*Start on the **1st day** of the following month after being hired\*
* 401k with Company match of up to **6%**!
* Life Insurance and Employee Assistance Program
* Company Paid Holidays


Compensation: $85,000\-$95,000 Depending Upon Experience


We are committed to a safe, drug\-free work environment and pre\-employment drug screening, physical and background checks are required prior to starting. **Candidates must be authorized to work in the US.**

jobs.title: Environmental Project Manager - Remediation - 6 years min experience
jobs.description:
**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**  

AECOM is actively seeking a talented Environmental Project/Program Manager for immediate employment in our Oakland, California office. In this role, you will be making a positive impact in the community through rewarding projects within our Environmental Practices.


This hybrid position (office and remote) requires the ideal candidate to demonstrate experience in regulatory and client engagement on complex sites, as well as investigation and remediation project experience, all while maintaining a strong emphasis on health and safety. The candidate should be detail\-oriented, possess excellent written and verbal communication skills, and be capable of working independently while collaborating within a high\-performance team.


Working at AECOM means being part of a global team and collaborating with award\-winning professionals worldwide. In this position, you will also be responsible for supporting business development for the Oakland office, technical delivery, stakeholder engagement and communication, and financial management.

**Responsibilities for this position may include the following:**

**Project/Program Management:**

* Oversee the management of projects, assisting in the establishment of project\-specific objectives and policies.
* Oversee the management the program for the portfolio of projects, assisting in the establishment of program specific processes and procedures.
* Understand site investigation and remediation techniques to drive effective solutions for our utility client.
* Engage with existing and potential clients to discuss AECOM service capabilities and expand the services provided.
* Ensure all aspects of the project portfolio align with design, budget, and schedule requirements.
* Provide technical oversight and quality control throughout the project lifecycle.
* Define project scope and objectives clearly.
* Manage all phases of projects from initiation to closeout.
* Anticipate resource needs and manage resources effectively.
* Exercise decision\-making authority while recognizing risks and uncertainties, implementing plans to mitigate them.
* Provide consistent project updates to various stakeholders regarding strategy, adjustments, and progress.
* Identify, mitigate, and manage project risks effectively.
* Manage complex client relationships and projects.
* Consistently deliver profit margins as planned.

 **Qualifications** **Minimum Requirements:**

* BS in engineering, geology, environmental science, or a related field with 6\+ years of experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
* US Citizen or US Permanent Resident. Sponsorship at this time or in the future is not eligible for this role.
* This role is subject to a background check.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* 10\+ years of experience in site investigation, remediation, project management, and business development.
* 2\+ years of experience managing a portfolio of projects and leading a team for a major client.
* Licensed in the State of California (Professional Engineer or Geologist).
* Experience working with state regulatory agencies in the states referenced for licensure.
* Proven experience in scheduling resources to ensure timely and budget\-compliant project delivery.
* Background in business development.
* Current 40\-hour HAZWOPER certification, including 8\-hour Supervisor training.
* PMP certification.
* Experience with regulatory and stakeholder negotiations.
* Proven track record of successfully managing environmental projects for various types of clients.
* Detail\-oriented with strong organizational and communication skills, both verbal and written.
* Superior communication, writing, editing, and reporting skills for diverse audiences.
* Experience preparing proposals, cost estimates, schedules, and change orders.

  

**Additional Information**  

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. ***To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in\-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.***

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD\&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well\-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

**Summary**


The Environmental Compliance Specialist is responsible for driving environmental compliance programs, conducting inspections and risk assessments, coordinating environmental activities, and leading training and corrective actions. This role emphasizes technical support, regulatory knowledge, and cross\-functional collaboration without direct management responsibilities.

**Essential Functions of the Job**

  

* Manage and oversee local, state, and federal environmental regulations and Luxfer policy. Proactively research and maintain awareness of changes in regulations and facilitate communication with relevant stakeholders.
* Drive an environmentally responsible culture within the organization. Develop and execute programs through partnerships with engineering, maintenance, and operations.
* Maintain and enhance the facilities ISO 14001 Certification
* Lead regulatory agency interactions, permit evaluation and processing, and new process and technology introduction.
* Ensure work performed by contractors, consultants, and employees is completed in accordance with Luxfer standards.
* Drive environmental metrics
* Build collaborative relationships with various stakeholders to ensure risks are identified early and managed appropriately.
* Submit time\-critical reports to various governmental agencies.
* Complete thorough and accurate environmental incident investigations and accompanying regulatory reports and develop appropriate corrective actions.
* Conduct regular environmental audits to assess compliance, identify areas for improvement, and implement corrective actions in collaboration with local operations leadership and teams.
* Develops and oversees waste management programs, including hazardous waste disposal.
* Provide training to employees on environmental policies, procedures, and best practices, fostering a culture of environmental responsibility.
* Coordinates environmental impact assessments for new projects, operations, or changes to existing processes, ensuring potential environmental risks are identified and mitigated.
* Prepare and submit required environmental reports to regulatory agencies, stakeholders, and internal management.
* Partner with Safety Manager on overlapping programs. Serve as a back\-up for Safety Manager.

**Job Skills and Requirements**

* Technical Knowledge of EPA Regulations, Hazardous Waste Management, relevant Environmental Programs (including but not limited to SWPPP, SPCC, HAZCOM), Environmental Permits and Recordkeeping
* Strong Analytical and problem\-solving skills.
* Attention to detail
* ISO 14001 Internal Auditor Certification Preferred
* Strong project management and organizational skills
* Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities.
* Certifications in environmental management (e.g., CEM, CHMM) are a plus.
* Strong knowledge and utilization of Microsoft Office products.
* Experience with CERS and SMARTS CA specific web based environmental solutions

**Education/Training Requirements**

* 3\+ years of increasing responsibilities in environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations experience
* Bachelor's Degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Engineering, or related field of study highly preferred.
